text: Meeting deadlines can be challenging, but good strategies help. Start with time management: break projects into smaller tasks and set mini-deadlines. This prevents last-minute panic. Prioritization is equally important. Identify which tasks are urgent or important and focus on those first. If the workload feels overwhelming, consider scope management. This means clarifying what the project actually requires and saying no to extra requests that don’t add value. Finally, communication is key. If you see a deadline is unrealistic, let your team or manager know early. They may adjust expectations or offer support. With these skills, deadlines become manageable rather than stressful.
